title: Where ZPA access evidence lives: console, client, connector, log streaming

prose.text: Evidence comes from the Admin Console, the client, the connector hosts and streamed logs, and each has its own limits.

prose.label: Console and retention.
prose.text: The retention of the logs the console shows is in [[zpa.log-receivers.delivery]]. Connector state and update status are in [[zpa.app-connectors.health]] and [[zpa.app-connectors.upgrades]].

prose.label: Client.
prose.text: {{ztunnel-versions}} {{posture-frequency}} The default cadence is also in [[zpa.posture-profiles.evaluation:cadence]]. The state indicator and local error codes of the client are not sourced {{gap:client-local-signals}}.

prose.label: Connector hosts.
prose.text: {{health-monitoring-tcp-failures}} An enrollment failure from a copied key is described in [[zpa.app-connectors.provisioning-keys]]. What the connector logs for reachability and certificate failures is not sourced {{gap:connector-log-signals}} Remote troubleshooting can collect logs and interfaces: {{journalctl-july14}} For App Connectors, see [[zpa.app-connectors.deployment:get-network-interfaces-july13]].

prose.label: Streamed logs.
prose.text: The fields are in [[zpa.troubleshooting.log-fields]], and the connector-side loss behavior in [[zpa.app-connectors.health]].

checks.do: How old the event is against the retention of the console and of any stream before looking for it.
Which tunnel type the client uses, since only Z-Tunnel 2.0 carries all ports and protocols.
How often the client evaluates posture for the profile in the policy, and that some checks evaluate immediately.
Whether a connector shows Disconnected while its VM runs, and what the connector reports locally.
That TCP failures and resets toward the application server are expected from health monitoring before treating them as the fault.
Whether a connector shows a copied-key enrollment failure in its console.
Whether streamed logs cover the period, noting the loss behavior.

health-monitoring-tcp-failures.statement: The help calls many TCP failures from an App Connector to the application server normal, mostly the result of the connector's health monitoring of the server, and says a capture facing the server shows many TCP handshakes and RST packets.

quotes: These TCP failures are normal and are mostly due to the App Connector doing health monitoring of the application server.
You can see a lot of TCP 3-way handshakes and/or RST packets if you get a pcap from the App Connector facing the application server.

ztunnel-versions.statement: Z-Tunnel 2.0 uses DTLS or TLS to send packets to the Zscaler service and can send all ports and protocols, while Z-Tunnel 1.0 forwards via CONNECT requests and sends all proxy-aware traffic or port 80/443 traffic, depending on the forwarding profile.

quotes: Z-Tunnel 2.0 has a tunneling architecture that uses DTLS or TLS to send packets to the Zscaler service.
Because of this, Z-Tunnel 2.0 is capable of sending all ports and protocols.
Z-Tunnel 1.0 sends all proxy-aware traffic or port 80/443 traffic to the Zscaler service, depending on the forwarding profile configuration.
Z-Tunnel 1.0 forwards traffic to the Zscaler cloud via CONNECT requests, much like a traditional proxy.

posture-frequency.statement: Zscaler Client Connector evaluates device posture for each posture type at a configured frequency, in one-minute intervals, with a maximum default of 15 minutes and a minimum of 2 minutes (Windows 4.4 and later, macOS 4.5 and later), and for some checks it evaluates immediately when the posture changes, whatever the frequency.

quotes: select how often Zscaler Client Connector evaluates device posture by selecting a value, in one-minute intervals, from the drop-down menu.
The maximum default value is 15 minutes. The minimum value is 2 minutes.
evaluates device posture immediately when the posture changes on a device, regardless of what is configured in the Frequency (In Minutes) field
Applies to Zscaler Client Connector version 4.4 and later for Windows and Zscaler Client Connector version 4.5 and later for macOS. For each posture type,
For the following posture checks, Zscaler Client Connector evaluates device posture immediately when the posture changes on a device

posture-frequency.conditions: The help gives the frequency as a per-posture-type setting with a maximum default of 15 minutes; the cadence subject cites the device posture article's every-15-minutes wording.

journalctl-july14.statement: The July 14, 2026 release summary lists support for the journalctl command for App Connectors, Private Service Edges, Private Cloud Controllers, and Network Connectors to collect service logs or full system logs for remote troubleshooting.

quotes: Private Access (ZPA) supports the journalctl command for App Connectors, Private Service Edges, Private Cloud Controllers, and Network Connectors to collect service logs or full system logs for remote troubleshooting.

client-local-signals.title: Client tunnel state and local error codes
client-local-signals.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Z-Tunnel state: ZCC must be in an active tunnel state for Private Access traffic interception. A user-accessible tunnel state indicator is available in the ZCC application. Error codes from ZCC: ZCC exposes local error codes on connection failure. These are ZCC-level diagnostics and are outside the ZPA admin console view." No captured source describes a tunnel state indicator for Private Access or says that error codes are produced on a connection failure; the legacy pointer to the Client Connector error-code article is a navigation aid and is not carried over.

connector-log-signals.title: What the connector logs for reachability and certificate failures
connector-log-signals.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Application reachability: the connector performs DNS and TCP reachability checks for applications at access time (or continuously if `health_reporting = CONTINUOUS`). Connection failures to the application server surface in connector logs as TCP or TLS errors against the application's IP/port. Certificate errors: if the application server's certificate chain fails validation by the connector (relevant for double-encrypted segments), the connector logs a TLS handshake failure." The connector health subject holds the sourced connectivity checks and messages, and the help says TCP failures toward the server are normal health monitoring (health-monitoring-tcp-failures); no source states these log contents or that the connector logs reachability failures by application.

remote-collection.title: Remote log and interface collection
remote-collection.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Remote troubleshooting supports `journalctl` collection of either service logs or full-system logs from App Connectors, Private Service Edges, Private Cloud Controllers, and Network Connectors. For App Connectors, the **Get Network Interfaces** command collects the network-interface inventory used by the connector." The release-summary capture that held this text was replaced by a canonical recapture that no longer contains it, The connector and Private Service Edge troubleshooting articles mention remote troubleshooting session commands that a paused component may reject, but neither mentions journalctl collection of service or full-system logs or a Get Network Interfaces command.
remote-collection.resolution: journalctl collection is in the release summary (claim journalctl-july14); the App Connector Get Network Interfaces command is claim get-network-interfaces-july13 in zpa.app-connectors.deployment.
